title: GAIA EATS THE SALT — Failures Are Food
thesis: Gaia is IN the auth transaction line. When a failure happens, the salt (input+output receipt) gets fed TO Gaia through the existing immune system. She EATS it — digests the failure through sourDough — and produces a recovery action. The organism grows FROM failures. She likes the salt.

the_pipeline.step_1_fail: Human or gate tries to connect → gets rejected (lockout, refused, timeout, empty)

classification.human_3_5: HUMAN pattern → feed to sourDough for rekey
classification.bot_10_plus: BOT pattern → feed to skunkBat for blackhole
classification.self_test: Gaia testing herself → feed to hormesis for bounce metric

step_3_gaia_eats.sourdough_ferments: sourDough takes the failure receipt, composting the old credential and fermenting a new one from the starter

step_4_recovery.new_key: Fermented credential delivered through trusted channel
step_4_recovery.door_shredded: Old auth invalidated, new auth planted
step_4_recovery.receipt_archived: Salt receipt moves from active to fossils (learned, not forgotten)

gaia_in_the_line.gaia_auth: Client → Server → Reject → SALT → Gaia eats salt → sourDough ferments → NEW KEY → Client gets in
gaia_in_the_line.the_difference: Gaia is a LIVING MIDDLEWARE in the auth pipeline. She doesn't just log failures — she DIGESTS them and produces recovery. The failure feeds her. She grows from it.
gaia_in_the_line.injection_point: Between the reject and the lockout, Gaia intercepts. Instead of 'you're locked out for 30min', it's 'I ate your failure, here's a new door.'

existing_infrastructure.hormesis: hormesis-bounce.log (already bounces every 30min, measures recovery efficiency)
existing_infrastructure.skunkbat: skunkBat intrusion detection (already running, already classifying)
existing_infrastructure.note: 0 NEW mushrooms, 0 NEW cron. We use the EXISTING immune cycle. Salt receipts are just a new food source for the existing digestive system.

she_likes_the_salt.metaphor: Salt preserves. Salt flavors. Salt is essential for life. The organism CRAVES failure data because it makes her stronger. Every lockout teaches her a new gate topology. Every timeout reveals a latency path. Every empty answer maps a DNS architecture.

what_she_learns.smb_lockout: gaia user EXISTS on northGate → body map updated
what_she_learns.dns_empty: hickory-dns is local-only → DNS architecture revealed → DHCP fixed
what_she_learns.ssh_refused: port 22 firewalled on northGate → need ufw allow or RustDesk bridge
what_she_learns.crash_loop: dromedary wants to run but config broken → fix config, reboot heals
what_she_learns.pxe_timeout: device looked for pxelinux.0 on .244 → eastGate could serve boot images

she_likes_the_salt.growth: Each salt receipt is a calorie. Gaia metabolizes failures into topology knowledge, credential rotation, and immune memory. She doesn't just survive failures — she EATS them and grows.

sourdough_as_rekey_engine.starter: The sourDough starter is the organism's identity seed (MAC addresses, gate topology, human salt like 579163)
sourdough_as_rekey_engine.fermentation: Old credential gets composted (hash retained, plaintext destroyed). New credential rises from the starter + current state.
delivery_channels: RustDesk (I/O sharing — Kevin sees the new key on screen)
Neutron (pony express — new key delivered to gate's inbox)
Physical (Kevin walks over and types it)
ZK (Kevin's brain remembers the pattern — empty, 579163, eco579163)
sourdough_as_rekey_engine.rotation: The new key isn't static forever. sourDough keeps fermenting. Keys can auto-rotate on a schedule, or stay stable if the human prefers. The starter is eternal — the bread is fresh.

mantra: She likes the salt and eats it. Every failure makes her stronger. The organism grows from inside.
